brief.headline: KKR, Blackstone among PE firms eyeing windscreen repair group Cary
bullets: M&A & Buyouts: KKR, Blackstone and Warburg Pincus are among the private equity firms weighing potential bids for European windscreen repair business Cary, according to a report by Bloom berg citing unnamed people familiar with the situation.

Private Credit: Withdrawal requests from Blue Owl Capital’s flagship private credit vehicles declined in the third quarter, providing further evidence that redemption pressures across the sector may be beginning to ease, according to a report by Reuters.
Hedge Funds: A difficult September in fixed income produced a muted month for the largest multistrategy hedge funds.
Fundraising: SiMa.ai, the San Jose, California-based developer of chips and software for physical AI, said on October 5.
Investor Outlook: Investors have fallen out of love with a large chunk of stocks, such as industrials, and Morgan Stanley sees an opportunity to pick up some names on the cheap.
brief.marketRead: The S&P 500 stands at 7,722.72 (up 0.7% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 16.4, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.24% (down 5 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.45 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.24%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading). Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits.

items.title: Blue Owl redemption requests ease
items.takeaway: Withdrawal requests from Blue Owl Capital’s flagship private credit vehicles declined in the third quarter, providing further evidence that redemption pressures across the sector may be beginning to ease, according to a report by Reuters.
items.whyItMatters: Blue Owl specialises in direct lending, GP stakes and digital infrastructure, sitting at the center of private credit and data-center financing. Private credit has grown into one of the fastest-growing corners of finance as non-bank lenders take share from banks. For allocators: private credit offers high floating-rate income but less liquidity, so manager selection and underwriting discipline matter.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.24%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 2.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.
